items.action: On every `<ds-split-button>` whose `menuItems` can be empty, pass the items or replace the control with `<ds-button>`.
items.appliesWhen: Only a `<ds-split-button>` that renders with `menuItems` empty — a list filled after the first render, a list built by a filter that can return nothing, or a split button used for one action. A split button whose items are always present behaves exactly as before.
items.pitfall: Nothing errors and the main button keeps working, so this is only visible on the chevron: it is disabled while the list is empty. Items fetched after the first render therefore leave a disabled chevron for as long as the fetch takes, which reads as a broken control to anyone who does not know it is waiting. Render the split button once the items are in hand, or keep the interval deliberately.
items.note: The chevron previously opened a `ds-menu` with nothing in it. It is now disabled while `menuItems` is empty and enables itself when items arrive — disabled rather than hidden, so the control keeps its geometry either way. A development build warns and names `ds-button` as the control for a single action. The panel can only ever be the `ds-menu` built from `menuItems`; anything else composes from `ds-button` and `ds-popover`.
items.verify: A split button with an empty `menuItems` shows a disabled chevron and opens no panel, and one with items opens its menu as before.

items.action: None to make it work. If you set `--focus-ring-inner` to a colour of your own to get a visible ring back, remove that override — it now fights the default. Keep it only on a scope whose ground is genuinely neither the surface nor the canvas.
items.appliesWhen: Every focused control in the library, because both focus roles compose from this token. Nothing else reads it, and no component token changes name or type.
items.pitfall: The gap is OPAQUE, so it paints the surface colour rather than letting the real ground through. On a control standing on a tinted band or an image the gap is a surface-coloured rim, not a hole — the same class of mismatch that made the previous value `--surface-canvas` draw a dark rim around a light card. Only `outline` + `outline-offset` gives a see-through gap, and a box-shadow token cannot carry an outline.
items.note: `--focus-ring-inner` was `transparent`, which paints nothing and reserves nothing, so the outer layer filled the whole 4px and the ring rendered as one solid brand band flush against the control — invisible against a brand-filled button and a heavy frame on a light one. It is `var(--surface-default)` again, so the ring is 2px of brand held 2px off the control, which is what the token has always described.
items.verify: Focus a solid-filled button and an outline button: both show a thin brand ring separated from the control by a gap, and the solid one is no longer distinguishable only by being slightly larger.
